output.headline: Demo Hawks fall 4-3; focus on two-strike approach, plate coverage, and pitcher recovery
what_decided_it: Riverside's 2-run inning 4 was their only big inning; Demo Hawks struck out 9 of 26 plate appearances (35%) and committed 2 errors.
strengths: Pitchers recorded 7 strikeouts while allowing only 3 walks; team on-base rate was 35% with 6 hits and 3 walks.

priorities.title: Protect the plate with two strikes
priorities.why: Team struck out 35% of plate appearances (9 of 26), and the game ended with consecutive strikeouts.

drills.title: Soft toss: two-strike outside corner
drills.description: Partner kneels off to the side and tosses to the outer half. Hitter works a two-strike approach: later start, compact finish, ball to the opposite field.
drills.safety_notes: Tosser stays outside the swing arc and wears a helmet. Stop the round if tosses drift toward the hitter’s hands.

insights.insight: With two strikes, protect the zone: widen what you'll swing at, shorten the swing, choke up slightly, and try to put the ball in play or foul off tough pitches.

priorities.title: Crowd the plate to reach outside pitches
priorities.why: Youth pitchers often miss away, and too many at-bats ended on outside pitches; moving closer brings those pitches into reach.

drills.title: Tee: two-strike outside corner
drills.description: From a tee on the outer half, hitters take a slightly shorter two-strike swing and drive the ball the other way. Five quality reps, then switch.
drills.safety_notes: Set the net so missed balls cannot reach a walkway. Helmet on for every swing.

insights.insight: Many youth pitchers miss away from the batter on purpose, because they don't want to hit anyone. Moving closer to the plate (crowding it) brings those outside pitches into reach.

priorities.title: Respect pitcher rest and recovery
priorities.why: J Ortiz #12 threw 71 pitches and is eligible 2026-10-22; M Chen #7 threw 34 pitches and is eligible 2026-10-19, so neither pitches before those dates.

drills.title: Between-outing recovery circuit
drills.description: Light movement, band work, and a short catch progression the day after a high-pitch outing. Stop at any sharp elbow or shoulder pain and check rest rules before the next live inning.
drills.safety_notes: This is recovery, not a bullpen. No max-effort throws. Pair with the pitcher’s remaining rest days.

insights.insight: Follow pitch counts and rest days, don't pitch on three days in a row, avoid catching on non-pitching days, and take time off from throwing each year.

lesson.title: A game built on failure
lesson.principle: In baseball, succeeding about 30% of the time at the plate can make a Hall of Fame career at the professional level. That's a 70% failure rate. You will not win every competition, and you will not lose every competition, but you will learn and grow through every competition.
lesson.life_lesson: Failing often on the way to success is normal in anything worth doing; what matters is learning from each try.

output.team_talk: We competed hard and gave ourselves a chance until the final out. One inning or one at-bat does not define this team—we win and lose together, and every player matters. Let's keep believing in each other and get back to work this week.
at_home: Let your player talk first on the ride home and say, 'I love watching you play.'
Praise effort and approach, not the scoreboard, and leave technique to the coach at a calm, agreed time.
